title: bev_fusion_lane_center: camera + radar BEV features -> lane-centre-line graph on an SD-map route
subtitle: Delivered chain of the registry systems champion / fast_recall / recall (D7 builder, one growth level). Snake layout: row 1 left to right, row 3 right to left, row 5 left to right, row 7 right to left. Orange = a choice inside the network, red = post-processing without a gradient path.

select.label: choice inside the network (gradient through the picked items, not the choice)

alt.label: optional or control (not in the registry chain)

nodes.label:
Optional front stages
gate, map net, registration
nodes.note: learned memory gate (2.1 ms, not in the timed total), SD map as five extra channels, soft FFT registration + trust; evaluated on failure series, no registry entry

nodes.label:
Hard trust gate
map x (trust >= 0.62)
nodes.note: optional, off the delivered chain
nodes.why: the SD-map raster is multiplied by 1 or 0 depending on a threshold on the learned trust (p18_regmap.py:46-47); registration recovers about half of the gap between no map and an exact map (E213)
nodes.replace_with: multiply by the trust probability itself (the trust head already outputs a number in [0, 1]) and train the builder with it
nodes.catch: the soft version has to be trained with map faults in the loop (wrong map 10 %, no map 10 %) or it over-trusts a wrong map

nodes.label:
Control: E94 trace network
628 ms, graphs stored
nodes.note: the matched reference of every comparison (registry kind graphs) and the earlier rule systems; not part of the delivered chain

nodes.label:
6 cameras + radar
(nuScenes)
nodes.note: 255 scenes, scene-disjoint splits TRAIN 8,414 / VAL 873 / TEST 833 frames

nodes.label:
GaussianCaR
frozen foundation
nodes.note: camera + radar BEV features, decoder PCA 32 + 7 map logits = 39 channels at 200 x 200, 0.5 m, cached
nodes.why: extracted once with frozen weights (about 0.4 s per frame on the RTX 3060); the 17-24 ms of the chain start from the cached features, so the delivered system from raw sensors is not that fast
nodes.replace_with: an image-radar BEV encoder trained inside the chain, or a small student distilled from GaussianCaR (the same direction as D26 for bev_fusion: the image features become trainable)
nodes.catch: any replacement has to fit the speed budget or the headline claim changes; the cache is what makes the loop cheap

nodes.label:
Dense lane head
U-Net heat + direction
nodes.note: trained separately, train rows from 3-fold out-of-fold heads, cached; its forward is not run by evaluate.py or the timing driver (old cost 5-8 ms)
nodes.why: its maps are stored arrays; no gradient from the builder or the graph ever reaches it
nodes.replace_with: fold it into the builder stem and train both together, the dense loss kept as an auxiliary
nodes.catch: the builder was tuned on out-of-fold maps; joint training has to keep train rows from seeing their own labels

nodes.label:
42-channel input
z-score + concat
nodes.note: 39 normalised channels + heat + direction

nodes.label:
Builder stem
conv pyramid
nodes.note: initialised from the control run e94_a, fine-tuned at 0.3x learning rate; features at 200, 100 and 50 cells

nodes.label:
Seed spray
lattice 5 m + snap
nodes.note: fixed lattice, 25 offset samples per node, learned validity, snap and direction

nodes.label:
Seed selection
greedy NMS 3 m, K0
nodes.note: K0 = 96 or 144 seeds
nodes.why: a greedy distance NMS with an argmax loop on detached scores (p16_builder.py:289-295)
nodes.replace_with: a learned objectness gate under a budget loss, or a Gumbel top-k with a straight-through estimate; or no selection: every lattice seed grows a gated branch
nodes.catch: K0 sets the frame time; soft gating over all lattice seeds costs a multiple of the compute

nodes.label:
Context + ray read-out
verified rays
nodes.note: graph-biased self-attention over all tips, 12 rays x <= 5 samples per tip, survival T = cumprod of the verification probabilities

nodes.label:
Child choice
argmax + endpoint NMS
nodes.note: b = 3 children per tip
nodes.why: last verified sample per ray by argmax, then dominance and a greedy endpoint NMS (p16_geom.py:104, 135-140); inputs detached
nodes.replace_with: a softmax / sparsemax or straight-through Gumbel over the ray samples, and a learned suppression score instead of the greedy endpoint NMS
nodes.catch: the picked items already carry gradient (header of p16_builder.py); a soft choice mainly changes credit assignment, at the cost of gradients for every sample

nodes.label:
Child tokens
rescoring layer
nodes.note: a transformer layer over parent and siblings re-scores the child validity (stage_c)

nodes.label:
Beam top-M
+ link top-k
nodes.note: M = 288 / 144 seeds (champion, recall) or 192 / 96 (fast_recall)
nodes.why: topk(M) on detached path validity (p16_geom.py:153) keeps M nodes per direction; the link head sees only the 6 nearest ends inside a cone (p16_builder.py:541-546)
nodes.replace_with: soft top-k by optimal transport (Xie et al. 2020), or a learned keep gate trained with the vertex-budget loss (vc_penalty exists, weight 0)
nodes.catch: M sets the frame time; a soft budget has to be annealed to a hard cut at test time unless the gate trains to saturate

nodes.label:
Link head
forward x backward ends
nodes.note: link logit between ends of different seeds, connector verification

nodes.label:
Time recursion
prior + hard match
nodes.note: champion and recall only; fast_recall runs without it
nodes.why: the previous frame is run through the same builder, its top 64 nodes are warped by the ego motion and fused when a hard test (1.5 m, 30 deg) matches; costs +5.9 ms; the repo says its value is stability, not the single-frame score (E123, E132, E196)
nodes.replace_with: carry the previous node tokens as a recurrent state and attend to them (the learned memory gate is the pixel-level version) instead of re-running the builder and matching
nodes.catch: no measured gain to protect, so the replacement only has to be cheaper and no less stable

nodes.label:
Alive filter + export
tau 0.7, sort
nodes.note: first step of assemble(): CUDA-graph replay, copy to numpy, then numpy / numba
nodes.why: nodes with validity > 0 and path validity >= 0.7 are kept and sorted (p16_infer.py:564-577); tau 0.7 was fixed on VAL
nodes.replace_with: a keep gate trained to saturate (the survival loss exists), so the threshold is the gate's own 0.5
nodes.catch: calibration of the gate under failure (cameras off, wrong map)

nodes.label:
Path union
snap + split on edge
nodes.note: 16 % of the assembly time; the numba kernels are bit-identical to the python version (E216)
nodes.why: merges the beam nodes into one graph: reuse a vertex within 1.5 m, else snap onto the nearest edge within 0.5 m and split it, else a new vertex; link probability >= 0.5 makes an edge
nodes.replace_with: learned node merging: a soft assignment of nodes to vertices (differentiable clustering or graph coarsening) with the link head predicting same-vertex; the snap itself stays as the differentiable closest-point projection onto a segment, with soft radius gates
nodes.catch: exact edge splitting at foot points is geometry and should stay exact; learn only the merge decision

nodes.label:
Clean-up
bubbles, spurs
nodes.note: E259.b0: switched off on 7 models it adds 0.44 to 0.73 vertices per 100 m, so it stays
nodes.why: graph walks remove duplicate bubbles under 2.5 m and spurs under 5 m, keeping the branch of highest mean validity
nodes.replace_with: an edge-keep head (message passing over the union graph) trained with the graph losses, plus the duplicate penalty (dup_geo) so that the builder stops emitting bubbles
nodes.catch: the vertex budget is part of the headline, so the learned step has to match the 14.3 per 100 m

nodes.label:
Junction anchoring
heat peaks -> split
nodes.note: E258.a0: off costs Q -0.0004 and J -0.0042 on fast_recall (about 1.0 ms saved): registry fast_recall_na runs without it
nodes.why: junction-heat peaks (maximum filter 9) split the nearest edge at the foot point and link free ends within 8 m and 100 deg
nodes.replace_with: give the junction heat to the link head as a feature and let the learned link decide
nodes.catch: carries almost nothing on fast_recall, so it is the first rule to drop, not to replace; champion is not covered by that measurement

nodes.label:
Fork relocation
move to heat peak
nodes.note: E258.a0: off costs Q -0.0111 and J -0.054 on fast_recall
nodes.why: moves a fork vertex up the trunk (at most 12 m) to the nearest junction-heat peak
nodes.replace_with: regress the fork position from the junction head (a sub-cell offset as in CenterPoint) and let the builder place the fork: a learned fork decision inside the builder
nodes.catch: needs a fork-position loss on the GT junction landmarks; the heat peak is also what the metric rewards

nodes.label:
Fork pruning
keep one branch
nodes.note: E215: J 0.265 -> 0.409, Q 0.701 -> 0.735, S 0.746 -> 0.769, F1@1 and lanes found unchanged: the largest measured gain of any rule step
nodes.why: at forks whose 3 x 3 junction heat is below 0.3 (champion) / 0.4 (recall) one branch keeps its continuation and the others get a copied vertex, geometry unchanged
nodes.replace_with: a learned continuation head: score continuation pairs at every junction and assign branches by a soft assignment (Sinkhorn), trained with the graph losses
nodes.catch: the replacement has to reproduce J 0.409 first; the rule is the reference to beat

nodes.label:
Piece cut
legacy chain walk
nodes.note: the legacy cut is kept because the route head and the consumer were trained on it (D24 open item)
nodes.why: degree-based chain walk turns vertices and edges into polyline pieces
nodes.replace_with: tokens per edge by message passing over the vertex-edge graph, so that the route head reads the graph and no cut is needed
nodes.catch: route head and consumer have to be retrained on the new tokens and route success measured again

nodes.label:
Douglas-Peucker
(*_dp systems only)
nodes.note: champion 14.8 -> 9.5, fast_recall 15.0 -> 9.9 node ids per 100 m, Q -0.0005 (E257, D20); off by default, not in the timed chain
nodes.why: polylines simplified with a 0.2 m tolerance, ends and junction ids kept
nodes.replace_with: a learned vertex gate under a vertex-count loss
nodes.catch: the budget of 14.3 per 100 m is on the per-piece basis; node-id counts are quoted separately (D25)

nodes.label: Ego poses
nodes.note: exact nuScenes poses; feed the time recursion and the consumer

nodes.label:
Junction head
split / merge heat
nodes.note: reads the stem features; its heat travels with the raw tree to anchoring, relocation and pruning (heat peaks alone find forks about as well as the control: split F1 0.42 against 0.35, E123)

nodes.label:
SD map
(ADASIS-like, simulated)
nodes.note: rasterised to 5 channels; the timing driver uses the exact map

nodes.label:
Lane graph
vertices, edges, pieces
nodes.note: the output of the piece cut (of Douglas-Peucker for *_dp); a function of the post-processing rules

nodes.label:
Route input
tokens along edges
nodes.note: gather and interpolation in numpy; each vertex takes the node of highest validity (hard); the route head is trained on stored token files

nodes.label:
Route head
SD-map attribute
nodes.note: route success champion 0.894 / 0.891 -> 0.899 / 0.900 with fork pruning (E215); builder frozen, tokens stored

nodes.label:
Planner consumer
ConsB
nodes.note: 6 m edge tokens + route probability + ego motion -> 8 ego-path points; path error floor 0.27 m whatever the graph (gap 3)

nodes.label:
Route flags
per lane point
nodes.note: lane-level assignment to the SD-map route, road level as fallback

nodes.label:
Builder losses
matching-free
nodes.note: per head and per level on network outputs: ray verification, child position, child validity, edge precision + soft-min recall, junction, link; no loss sees the assembled graph

nodes.label:
Training entry points
and search
nodes.note: builder, dense head, route head and consumer are trained in separate pieces

nodes.label: Data, GT and prep
nodes.note: features, ground-truth fields, splits, SD-map library, route targets

nodes.label:
Joint builder + route
fine-tune (closed)
nodes.note: the one end-to-end attempt: the assembly runs inside the loop and the route loss reaches the node tokens only, not positions, validity or edges; negative three times (E202, E214, E232), not adopted

groups.label: assemble(): numpy / numba, no gradient path (alive filter above, piece cut and Douglas-Peucker included)

not_drawn.training/bflc_paths.py: project paths from the checkout location, imported everywhere
not_drawn.training/models/p16_ref.py: numpy reference of the tree spec, the oracle of evaluation/tests/test_p16_spec.py
